findings.title: ADR-0071 §5 still says the release-notes generator reads nothing but the register, the dependency list and the provisional Arabic files, and lists seven sections; since D-280 it also reads tools/release/release-notes-disclosures.json and writes an eighth section
findings.reproduction: On the candidate (source ddf42ccd2): (1) docs/architecture/adr/ADR-0071-p7-traceability-register-snapshot-about-release-notes-release-blockers-protocol-audit.md §5.1 ends 'It reads nothing else.' and §5.2 lists sections 1-7 (identity, counts, unfinished items, later clauses, external dependencies, provisional Arabic, Arabic summary); no amendment section exists (grep -n 'Amendment' on the file finds none). (2) tools/release/release-notes.mjs l.10 and l.28: 'It also reads its own checked-in input tools/release/release-notes-disclosures.json' (DEFAULT_DISCLOSURES). (3) docs/handover/release-notes.md l.71 '## Known limitations disclosed in this release' and its Arabic twin l.137, a section §5.2 does not list. (4) decisions.md D-280 records the orchestrator's acceptance 'instead of amending the ADR'.
findings.expected: The accepted ADR that specifies the generator (ADR-0071 §5.1, §5.2) describes its actual inputs and sections, through a dated amendment as the other P7 ADRs do (for example ADR-0064 Amendment 5, ADR-0065 Amendment 1), so that a maintainer who regenerates the release notes from the ADR's description gets the shipped output.
findings.actual: The ADR text and the shipped generator disagree on one input file and one output section. Behaviour is unaffected: release-notes.mjs --check exits 0 on the candidate and the disclosures section is correct (54-handover-tools.log). Raised afresh as the assignment directs; it is the same drift as the old branch's F-DG7-973, which was accepted there as an observation (D-280, D-281).

findings.title: The handover release notes and 25 register rows cite DG7 finding ids (F-DG7-913…971) that do not exist in this branch's findings.json, and the REQ-DLV-014 later clause names old-branch findings that validate --stage DG7 on this branch cannot show
findings.reproduction: On the candidate: (1) grep -c F-DG7 docs/delivery/findings.json -> 0 (D-281 reset DG7 findings for the clean re-gate). (2) docs/handover/release-notes.md l.35 (REQ-DLV-012 later clause) cites 'F-DG7-960's FE-C3 and F-DG7-920's DO-D8 handback'; l.36 (REQ-DLV-014 later clause) reads 'with each DG7 finding (round 2: 915, 935, 960-963) fixed and verified by a non-owner, shown by validate.mjs --stage DG7 at the gate'. (3) python3 csv reader over docs/delivery/requirements.csv: 25 rows' notes cite F-DG7-913, 914, 915, 920, 921, 935, 954, 955, 956, 960, 961, 962, 963, 971; none of the 25 notes, nor any docs/handover file, says that these ids live on the old branch (commit 1612f85fc). D-281 qualifies only path mentions ('Path mentions in register notes, handbacks and this file ... refer to commit 1612f85fc'), and decisions.md is not part of the handover.
findings.expected: Every finding id that the handover documents and the register cite resolves in the delivered findings register, or is explicitly qualified as an old-branch record (commit 1612f85fc, D-281); and each completes-after-gate clause names a condition that the DG7 gate on this branch can actually show.
findings.actual: A reader of the sealed package (release notes, register, findings.json) cannot resolve these ids, and the REQ-DLV-014 clause 'shown by validate.mjs --stage DG7' refers to findings that are not in this branch's findings.json, so the gate check is vacuous for them. No product behaviour is affected; the findings' substance was verified on the old branch.
